meta.title: Runtime Upgrade: Fix the Ticking Clock Once

views.label: Every cluster, not just old ones
views.note: Teams are frequently unaware they're several LTS generations behind — check the actual DBR version per cluster.

views.label: Newest LTS that fits, not newest overall
views.note: Target the newest LTS supporting required features, standardized across the estate to shrink the compatibility matrix.

views.label: EOL blocks cutover
views.note: A runtime already close to end-of-support gets skipped as a target baseline, not carried forward by default.

cards.title: Every workload, not the ones already flagged old
items: An old runtime carried into the target cloud unchanged just relocates a ticking clock
Check the actual DBR version per cluster and job — teams are often generations behind without knowing it
Migration is the natural forcing function to fix this once, not defer it again

cards.title: Standardize, don't just upgrade
items: Target the newest LTS supporting required features, not simply one version newer than source
Standardize on one or two runtime versions across the target estate
UC access-mode, serverless, and Photon requirements shift with every LTS release — verify current, don't hardcode

cards.title: EOL is a hard skip, not a soft preference
items: A source runtime close to its support end date should not become the target baseline by default
Do not migrate clusters or jobs on end-of-life runtimes — upgrade and validate before cutover
Re-check the release-notes page before relying on any dated support-window snapshot
